name: Abel
overview: Abel was a male figure in the early biblical narrative, identified as the son of Adam and Eve. He is uniquely noted as the first person to be murdered, an event that sets a significant precedent in Scripture. No tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Abel means 'morning mist,' reflecting perhaps the fleeting nature of his life. This proper name is recorded in Genesis 4:2 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Abel was the son of Adam and Eve and the brother of Cain. His brother Cain is recorded as the one who killed him, making their relationship central to his story.
scriptureSignificance: Abel holds a crucial place in the biblical account as the first martyr, whose righteous offering was accepted by God. His death at the hands of his brother Cain illustrates the tragic consequences of sin and jealousy. Abel’s faithful sacrifice prefigures the ultimate sacrifice of Christ and highlights God's attention to the heart and faith of His people.
